Field notes, dispatches, and quarterly entries.

A working journal of the foundry — site visits, methodology revisions, capital deployments, and the slow business of restoring degraded land. Updated as work allows; archived by fiscal quarter.

QUARTERLY LETTER
FIELD REPORT
CARDIGAN BAY
Three years on, the Cardigan Bay saltmarsh is holding sediment faster than projected.

The pilot reach at Mwnt has cleared its third growing season under managed inundation. Accretion ledgers — measured against the 2021 baseline — show 4.6 cm of net deposit, ahead of the 3.1 cm modelled. We log what shifted, what didn't, and what we expect to do differently in Q4.

READ THE FULL ENTRY

— Margaret Holloway, Field Lead

Q2 2024 ledger: 14,200 displaced acrosss 21 active sites, £4.8M on budget.

Beaver dam analogues at Glen Lowan: first measurable channel widening.
Twelve months in, the BDA cluster across the lower Lowan has produced visible structural change. Mean wetted width grew 38% above the 2022 baseline, with three new pools beginning to scour.

Year-three serviced audit, Loch Awe planting: 78.4% across 132,000 stems.
Five-fold sampling across the Loch Awe broadleaf reach indicates survival within the projected band. We log the failure clusters — boggy western edge, deer pressure on the north paddock — and revise the regime accordingly.

Peat re-wetting at Border Mires: water table holding within 8 cm of surface for 218 of 240 monitored days.
The bunding programme commissioned in 2021 continues to perform within design parameters. We log the brief excursions to lower table during the dry weeks of July, and discuss the implications.
